title: Sitting in with Sam Wooding; Charlie Dixon's Naughty Waltz
summary: Asked about Emperor Jones, Thomas denies it. He stopped by Sam Wooding's band at the Lenox Club, was put in the first chair and struggled through Charlie Dixon's Naughty Waltz.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Now what about this mention about work for a while with Emperor Jones.
Who?
Played for a while with Emperor Jones.
JT (2 of 1) 91
No.
That's wrong, huh?
No, no.
You worked for Sam Wooding at the (Lenox) Club?
No, I just had a stop by one night. Emperor Jones? That sounds like Charles Gilbert or Paul Robeson
He's not talking about Broadway Jones, is he?

I don't know. Anyhow, just stopped by one night and there's a tremendous musician by the name of Sam Wooding, he has the band there. And another helluva guy by the name of Charlie Dixon doing the arrangements, you know.
Oh, he was with Sam Wooding?

He's the arranger for Sam Wooding at that time. And musicians in those days they like to trick you. Say anything to you. Say, well, (?.) so and so. ... So they put me in the first chair. You know, dig this. And ... Famous arrangement of his stamped off the band.' called the Naughty Waltz.
Oh, yeah. LATER Chick Webb did play-that.
... I always thought that Webb, he thought I was one of the few guys of the Henderson band that made it swing, that's what he always told me.
How did you make out with this arrangement of the "Naughty Waltz?
JT (2 of 1) 92
Struggled through.
Well, I've always heard that about Charlie Dixon though that he wrote very tough stuff.
Oh, yeah. Very hard ... (inaudible)
And, how long were you with Sam Wooding?
I wasn't with Sam Wooding at all. I just stopped by.
Oh, I see.
